summary: The writer of a lean budget apologizes to employees who lose promised raises, and denies the city is in crisis.
realLife: After a council's tied vote killed a property tax increase, the member who drafted the lean substitute budget apologized to employees whose raises were dropped. She said the promise had been made without planning for later years. She rejected the word crisis, saying debts were paid, payroll was covered and no one was laid off. Backers of the tax warned that job losses could follow within a year, and opponents said the public had not been asked enough.
sources: WPLN (Nashville, Tennessee), 'Nashville council rejects property tax hike, finalizing budget that pinches schools and city staff', June 20, 2018: https://wpln.org/post/nashville-council-rejects-property-tax-hike-finalizing-budget-that-pinches-schools-and-city-staff/
